title: Bayesian model comparison across 293 spectra given one event: which model classes carry the posterior?
question: Assigning priors over model classes (elastic isoscalar/isovector operators x masses; inelastic O1/O4 x masses x delta incl. continuous delta) and marginalising the coupling, what is the posterior over models given the 248 keV event (b_H = 5.7e-4) and the low-energy null, how concentrated is it, what is the model-marginalised DM-vs-background Bayes factor (Bayesian LEE), and how does it depend on the model prior?
headline_result: Marginalising coupling and 298 distinguishable spectra gives B_DM = 16.4 (uniform over spectra) to 28.7 (class priors), a Bayesian trials factor B_max/B_DM = 10 below the best model's 171 that matches the frequentist N_eff = 12-14; the posterior is diffuse (65-99 effective models, top model 3.4%), 58-85% inelastic (O1v/O4 at delta >= 250 keV), 11-30% q^2-suppressed spin operators, < 1e-4 SI-like
key_numbers: B_DM log-uniform s: uniform spectra 16.4, 4 classes 28.7, physics-weighted 28.7, raw 469 models 13.7, heavy-only 28.0; uniform-s 6.6, Jeffreys 13.8, with rho 15.9, mu-prior 17.0; B_max/B_DM 10.3 (12.3 raw) vs N_eff 12.2/13.9, SBB cap 14.7; per model L10 71, O6 54, O10 30, O4 10, O1s 0.06, m<=50 GeV 0; L10 flat 30.6 vs P016 44.8 (N_M 1.16 vs 0.70); posterior 50%/90% in 15-29/64-90 models, exp(H) 65-99; P(inel) 0.58/0.85, P(delta>=300) 0.32/0.46, P(q2-spin) 0.30/0.11; continuous delta class B 45.7 vs grid 38.7, tuning penalty 2.4-10, O1s delta posterior 318-379 keV; predictive 6.76 t yr: model average 0.92 events P(0)=0.58 P(>=2)=0.20, top inelastic 2.3, background 0.0014
model_or_mechanism: P016 few-bin joint likelihood (200-270 keV bin n=1 b_H=5.695e-4; digitised Fig. 5 low-energy NR-band bins with theta nuisance; empty 125-200 keV bin) with exact coupling marginalisation L/L0 = e^-s (1 + rho s/b_H) W(mu) under log-uniform/uniform/Jeffreys priors on s or on total ROI events mu; in-window shape factor rho from 23 keV resolution; model priors uniform/classes/physics-weighted/raw/heavy; continuous-delta integration to the kinematic ceiling; posterior entropy; Poisson posterior predictive
stance: statistical reassessment (weakens: B_DM 16-29 vs 170 single-model, diffuse posterior; strengthens relative case for inelastic delta >= 250 keV and q^2-suppressed spin operators over SI-like couplings)
